note: Accepted differences from Excel and Google Sheets. Each entry is a decision, not a defect. A difference belongs here only after a reviewer confirms it is intentional or out of scope. Fixtures that assert current behaviour must link to an id here.

differences.detail: Excel applies a final-result rounding pass so =0.1+0.2 shows 0.3. This engine returns 0.30000000000000004.
differences.impact: Display only for most workbooks, but exact equality tests on computed values can disagree with Excel.

differences.summary: `;` is accepted as an argument separator.
differences.detail: Excel accepts `;` only under locales that use it. This engine always accepts both `,` and `;`.
differences.impact: Strictly more permissive, so no valid formula is rejected.

differences.detail: Excel reports a circular-reference warning and puts 0 in the cell. Google Sheets returns `#REF!`. This engine uses a distinct `#CIRCULAR!` marker.
differences.impact: The differential harness must normalise this before comparing.

differences.detail: The expansion is literal, so a whole-column reference materialises a million rows instead of using the used range.
differences.impact: Correct results, unusable performance. Tracked as a performance defect, not a compatibility one.
